chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Jelly Roll Morton at the Bandbox
summary: Morton played piano at the Bandbox, was loud-mouthed and surrounded by a crowd, but Holmes finds him a good, intelligent man.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: And where did you first run into Jelly Roll Morton? Was it at the Rhythm Club?

No, it was the Bandbox. He come in the Bandbox, and he was playing piano in there. Somebody said to me, 'That's Jelly Roll Morton.' I said, 'Jelly Morton? I never heard of him.' He was sittin' down there playin' the piano, Mister Jelly Lord. Mister Jelly Lord! I don't know what the hell can I say about him. Mister'Jelly Lord, don't come up with that old-time stuff! Heh-heh. After that, I met him, you know, and I found out who he was. He was all right. But he'd stand out on the corner and give all the musicians hell -- give everybody hell. He was a
loud-mouthed guy, you know. But he was all right.
Happy Caldwell told me he used to always have a crowd around him and...
Oh, he would always have a crowd.
...they'd egg him on and tell him 'You can't play piano' and...

Oh yeah, he would talk... Oh, he loved to play. Play and sing his numbers. Sure. Jelly was all right if you knew him. Yeah, Jelly Roll contributed a lot to music. Good guy. No dummy. He was not a dummy at all.
